cards.text: The writer of Hebrews is writing to believers. He's just told them to run their race with their eyes fixed on Jesus, and to take God's discipline the way a son does (Hebrews 12:1-13). Now he gets practical: pursue peace with everyone.

cards.question: Along with peace with everyone, what else does the writer tell them to pursue?

cards.text: Then he tells them to look out for each other. See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up.

cards.question: The writer warns against a root of bitterness springing up. What does he say it would do?

answers.text: Stay small and hurt no one

cards.text: Next: see to it that no one is sexually immoral, or godless like Esau, Jacob's older twin brother (Genesis 25:24-26). The writer reminds them that Esau sold his birthright.

cards.question: Esau sold his birthright. What does the writer say Esau sold it for?

cards.text: A birthright for one meal? That's like handing over the keys to your HOUSE for ONE cookie. Later, when Esau wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected.

cards.question: Esau could find no ground for repentance. True or false: He still sought the blessing with tears.

cards.text: Now the writer starts with what you have NOT come to: a mountain that can be touched, burning with fire. Friend, I stand next to hot ovens all day, and even I'm keeping my mustache WAY back from that one.

cards.question: The mountain you have not come to is burning with fire. What else does the writer say is there?

cards.text: Then comes a trumpet blast and a voice. The people who heard that voice begged that no further word be spoken.

cards.question: The people could not bear what was commanded (Exodus 19:12-13): if even an animal touches the mountain, it must be ___.
The sight at that mountain was terrifying. True or false: Moses, Israel's leader, stayed calm through it.

cards.text: Even Moses said, "I am trembling with fear." Friend, when the TOUR GUIDE is shaking, the tour is OVER.
Deep breath, baker, because the writer says that scary mountain is NOT where you've come. You've come to a different mountain.

cards.question: Instead of that terrifying mountain, where does the writer say you have come?

cards.text: You've come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels in joyful assembly. At the first mountain, people BEGGED for no further word, and here it's angels in JOY!

cards.question: On Mount Zion, you have come to the congregation of the firstborn, enrolled in ___.

cards.text: You have come to God the Judge of all and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect. And then the writer names Jesus.

cards.question: On Mount Zion, you have come to Jesus. What does the writer call Him?

answers.text: The mediator of a new covenant
The builder of a new temple
The keeper of the old law

cards.text: Last on the list is sprinkled blood. The writer sets it next to the blood of Abel, Adam's son, who was killed by his brother Cain (Genesis 4:1-8).

cards.question: True or false: The writer says the sprinkled blood speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.

cards.text: Then a warning: "See to it that you do not refuse Him who speaks." The writer points back to the people who refused Him who warned them on earth.

cards.question: The writer says if the people did not escape when they refused Him who warned them on earth, then what about rejecting Him who warns us from heaven?

answers.text: We will get a second warning

cards.text: Back then, His voice shook the earth. But now He has made a promise, and the writer quotes it from Haggai 2:6.

cards.question: His voice once shook the earth. True or false: Now He promises to shake the earth once more, and nothing else.
The writer says the words Once more mean created things will be removed. Why? So that the ___ may remain.

cards.text: What we're receiving is a kingdom that CAN'T be shaken. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer that got rattled every time somebody needed TAPE, so unshakable sounds like a DREAM to me.

cards.question: Since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, the writer says let us be filled with gratitude. How does he say we then worship God?

cards.text: The writer ends with a line from Deuteronomy 4:24: "For our God is a consuming fire."
